result.title: SkillBuffBench: Measuring What Agent Skills Contribute across Harnesses, Models, Skill Access Modes and Memory
result.comment: 18 pages, 2 figures, 6 tables. Work in progress: benchmark design and protocol; results to be added in a later version
result.summary: Agent Skills, file-based packages of procedural knowledge that a coding agent can discover and load on demand, are now shipped by every major agent harness, yet the evidence for how much they help comes almost entirely from settings in which the right Skill is hand-picked for the task and the agent starts from a blank slate. Neither holds in deployment, where an agent chooses from whatever library happens to be installed and frequently carries memory from earlier work. We present SkillBuffBench, a benchmark and paired evaluation protocol that treats Skill access as a three-level factor (no Skill, a curated Skill, and automatic invocation from an installed library), crosses it with memory (off and on), with four agent harnesses and with multiple models (the state-of-the-art proprietary models from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI, and the state-of-the-art open-weight models from Chinese providers), every model being run under every harness, and evaluates the result on research tasks contributed by domain experts together with the Skills they use, currently in materials science and biology, with the suite extended on a rolling basis. Every run is marked by a deterministic verifier; uncertainty is reported with a paired, task-level bootstrap; and cost, agent rounds and wall-clock time are reported alongside the score rather than folded into it. This version of the paper describes the design of the benchmark, its evaluation protocol and its current tasks and Skills. The evaluation is in progress: results will be added once the runs are complete, and the task suite, results and analysis will continue to be updated on a rolling basis.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SkillBuffBench 基准与配对评测协议，将 agent skill 的获取方式设为三级因素，并与记忆开关、多种 harness 与模型交叉，在材料科学与生物学专家任务上衡量技能的真实贡献，报告确定性验证得分及成本、轮次与耗时；当前版本仅描述设计与协议，结果待补。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「配对因素交叉、分离技能与记忆来源、成本单列」的评测设计可供核查，可能为区分 latent 推理步骤、视觉证据与记忆对 VLM 推理收益的各自贡献提供方法模板，但论文本身不涉及视觉或多模态内部状态。
